context:
Goal: Claude never reads or writes a file that may hold secrets, without needless refusals.
Problem (risk): the shell and read checks let .envrc, .env-prod and .env_local through while the editing tools refuse them, so a secret in one of those files can be read; only you can set which names count.
Based on (read): the editing tools refuse every name that starts with .env; shell commands and reads refuse only .env and .env.something.
Based on (read): the coordinator took the wider rule at 22:42 CST as a reversible pick, and PR #1057 builds it.
Departs from: today shell commands and reads refuse only .env and .env.something — the wider rule refuses every name that starts with .env, except .env.example, in every form.

options.gain: Secrets in .envrc, .env-prod or .env_local stay unread, whichever tool touches them.
options.how: Refuse every file whose name starts with .env, except .env.example, for edits, shell commands and reads alike, as PR #1057 builds.
options.label: Every .env name, in every form
options.lose: A harmless command such as making a folder named .envs, or a jq filter on .environment, is refused once and needs a retry.

options.gain: Fewer false refusals on names that only start with .env.
options.how: Narrow every form to .env and .env.something; drop the wider editing refusal.
options.label: Only .env and .env.something
options.lose: Writes to .envrc, which today's editing tools refuse, go through, and a secret there can be read.

reply: Routed 00:58 CST to lane refusal-uncited-rewrites: every name that starts with .env, except .env.example, is refused in every form, as PR #1057 builds.
title: Which file names count as secret env files that Claude never reads or writes?
why: Today the editing tools refuse any file whose name starts with .env, but shell commands and file reads refuse only .env and .env.something. So a file like .envrc is blocked one way and readable another. The coordinator picked the wider rule for now, which you have not seen; PR #1057 builds it.
